title: Empire of Brazil
capsule: The Empire of Brazil was established when Crown Prince Pedro declared independence from Portugal on 7 September 1822, was acclaimed Emperor Pedro I on 12 October, and was crowned on 1 December 1822; it was the only constitutional monarchy in the Americas to achieve stable long-term governance in the nineteenth century. Pedro I's autocratic tendencies prompted his abdication in 1831 in favour of his five-year-old son, whose long reign as Pedro II (1840–1889) oversaw the abolition of the slave trade (1850), mass European immigration, the Paraguayan War (1864–1870), and the gradual expansion of the coffee economy. The monarchy fell on 15 November 1889 when a military coup backed by republican and positivist civilian factions established a republic; Pedro II went peacefully into exile in Europe, where he died in 1891.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Brazilian imperial territory is well-bounded by diplomatic treaties with neighbouring states (notably the post-Paraguayan War settlement of 1872 and Barão do Rio Branco's late nineteenth-century arbitrations); the attested extent is among the most precisely documented of any nineteenth-century South American state.
